topics.title: Surah An - Naba part 1
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite Surah An - Naba verses 1 - 10.
The pupils should be able to explain the meaning of the great news mentioned in the surah.
The pupils should be able to identify the main themes in the first part of Surah An - Naba.

Introduction:
Today we will learn Surah An - Naba which means The Great News. This surah talks about important events that will happen on the Day of Judgment.

Content:
Surah An - Naba is the 78th surah of the Quran. The first verse says 'What will tell you what is the great news?' The great news refers to the Day of Judgment when Allah will judge all people. Allah describes heaven with rivers and fruits, and hell with fire and punishment. The surah reminds us that Allah created everything in pairs and made us from dust. We should remember that we will all be resurrected.

Class activity:
Pupils will form groups and take turns reciting the first 10 verses of Surah An - Naba with proper pronunciation.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is the meaning of Surah An - Naba?
2. Name two things Allah created in pairs.
3. What does the 'great news' refer to in this surah?
4. How should we prepare for the Day of Judgment?

Summary:
Surah An - Naba teaches us about the Day of Judgment and the importance of preparing for it by following Allah's commands.

topics.title: Surah An - Naba part 2
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite Surah An - Naba verses 11 - 30.
The pupils should be able to describe the events of the Day of Judgment as described in the surah.
The pupils should be able to explain the consequences for good and bad people on that day.

Introduction:
We continue learning Surah An - Naba which describes what will happen on the Day of Judgment. Last week we learned about the great news, today we will learn more details about that day.

Content:
The surah describes how people will be gathered for judgment. Allah will measure deeds with accurate scales. Those whose good deeds are heavy will go to Jannah (paradise) while those with heavy bad deeds will go to Jahannam (hell). The surah mentions that people will be divided into groups. Some will be happy in the highest levels of paradise, while others will be in the lowest depths of hell. Allah reminds us that this is certain to happen.

Class activity:
Pupils will draw a picture showing the Day of Judgment as described in Surah An - Naba, including the scales, paradise and hell.

Evaluation questions:
1. What will happen to people whose good deeds are heavy?
2. What will happen to people whose bad deeds are heavy?
3. What does Allah use to measure people's deeds?
4. Why should we be good according to this surah?

Summary:
Surah An - Naba teaches us about the certainty of the Day of Judgment and the importance of doing good deeds to enter paradise.

topics.title: Hadith on character
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite a hadith about good character.
The pupils should be able to explain the importance of good character in Islam.
The pupils should be able to create a personal plan to improve their character.

Introduction:
Today we will learn about hadith that teach us about good character. Character is how we behave and treat others. Islam teaches us to have good character in everything we do.

Content:
The Prophet Muhammad (SAW) said: 'The best among you are those who have the best character.' Good character includes being honest, kind, patient, and respectful to others. The Prophet also said: 'None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.' Good character is more important than religious acts without good intentions. We should be good to our family, friends, neighbors, and even people we don't know.

Class activity:
Pupils will write down three good character traits they want to develop and how they will practice them this week.

Evaluation questions:
1. What did the Prophet say about good character?
2. Name two examples of good character.
3. Why is good character important in Islam?
4. How can you show good character to your classmates?

Summary:
Good character is very important in Islam and we should all try to develop good character traits in our daily lives.

topics.title: Fiqh: sawm
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list the rules of fasting in Ramadan.
The pupils should be able to explain the benefits of fasting.
The pupils should be able to identify things that break the fast.

Introduction:
Today we will learn about sawm which means fasting in Islam. We know that fasting is one of the five pillars of Islam and is especially important during the month of Ramadan.

Content:
Fasting during Ramadan means not eating or drinking from dawn until sunset. We should also avoid bad behavior like lying, fighting, or using bad language. Fasting teaches us self - control and helps us remember Allah. Children who have reached puberty, adults who are healthy, and those who are not traveling must fast. People who are sick, elderly, pregnant, or breastfeeding may not fast but should make it up later. Things that break the fast include eating, drinking, smoking, and sexual relations during daylight hours.

Class activity:
Pupils will role - play different situations and discuss whether they break the fast or not.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is the time for fasting during Ramadan?
2. Name three things that break the fast.
3. Who is exempt from fasting?
4. What are the benefits of fasting?

Summary:
Fasting in Ramadan is an important act of worship that teaches us self - control and brings us closer to Allah.

topics.title: Fiqh: zakat
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain the rules of giving zakat.
The pupils should be able to calculate simple zakat amounts.
The pupils should be able to list who should receive zakat.

Introduction:
Today we will learn about zakat which is the third pillar of Islam. Zakat means giving a portion of our wealth to those in need. It is a way to purify our wealth and help others.

Content:
Zakat is 2.5% of our savings and wealth that we give to poor people each year. We must have a certain amount of money (nisab) before we pay zakat. The money should be saved for one lunar year. Zakat can be given to poor people, those in debt, travelers, and Islamic organizations. Allah says in the Quran that giving zakat purifies our wealth and makes it grow. When we give zakat, we are obeying Allah and helping our Muslim brothers and sisters who are in need.

Class activity:
Pupils will calculate zakat on different amounts of money like ₦10,000, ₦50,000, and ₦100,000.

Evaluation questions:
1. What percentage of our wealth do we give as zakat?
2. Who should receive zakat?
3. Why do we pay zakat?
4. What is the minimum amount of wealth needed before paying zakat?

Summary:
Zakat is an important pillar of Islam that helps purify our wealth and support those in need.

topics.title: Seerah: the Madinah community
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to describe how the Prophet built the Muslim community in Madinah.
The pupils should be able to explain the importance of community service in Islam.
The pupils should be able to give examples of how Muslims help each other.

Introduction:
Today we will learn about how the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) built the first Muslim community in Madinah. This community was based on brotherhood, cooperation, and helping each other.

Content:
When the Prophet and Muslims migrated to Madinah, they established a strong community based on Islamic principles. The Prophet created a brotherhood between the Muhajireen (migrants from Makkah) and Ansar (helpers from Madinah). They shared their wealth, food, and homes with each other. The Prophet also built the first mosque in Madinah which became the center of the community. Muslims worked together to build houses, farms, and businesses. They took care of the poor, orphans, and elderly. This community showed how Muslims should live together with love and cooperation.

Class activity:
Pupils will work in groups to create a poster showing how Muslims can help each other in their community today.

Evaluation questions:
1. Who did the Prophet create a brotherhood between in Madinah?
2. What was the center of the Madinah community?
3. How did Muslims in Madinah help each other?
4. Why is community service important in Islam?

Summary:
The Madinah community built by the Prophet shows us the importance of brotherhood, cooperation, and helping each other in Islam.

topics.title: Seerah: treaties and peace
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name the treaties the Prophet made with other groups.
The pupils should be able to explain the importance of peace in Islam.
The pupils should be able to describe how the Prophet chose peace over war when possible.

Introduction:
Today we will learn about the peace treaties the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) made during his life. Islam encourages peace and the Prophet showed us how to make peace even with those who were against him.

Content:
The Prophet made several important peace treaties during his life. The most famous is the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah with the people of Makkah. Even though the Muslims were strong, the Prophet chose to make peace instead of fighting. He said: 'Making peace is better than fighting.' Another important treaty was the Constitution of Madinah which established peace between different groups in the city. The Prophet taught that peace is better than war when possible, and that Muslims should be peaceful with those who are peaceful with them.

Class activity:
Pupils will role - play a peace negotiation between two groups, following the example of the Prophet's approach to peace.

Evaluation questions:
1. What was the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah?
2. What did the Prophet say about making peace?
3. Name another treaty the Prophet made.
4. Why is peace important in Islam?

Summary:
The Prophet Muhammad showed us that peace is important in Islam and that we should always try to make peace when possible.

topics.title: Islamic law basics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to differentiate between halal and haram.
The pupils should be able to give examples of halal and haram actions.
The pupils should be able to explain how Islamic law guides our daily choices.

Introduction:
Today we will learn about Islamic law basics, specifically the concepts of halal and haram. These words tell us what is allowed and what is not allowed in Islam.

Content:
Halal means something that is allowed or permitted in Islam. Haram means something that is forbidden or not allowed. For example, eating halal food is allowed while eating pork is haram. Praying five times a day is halal while missing prayer without excuse is haram. Islamic law comes from the Quran and Sunnah of the Prophet. It covers all aspects of life including what we eat, how we dress, how we behave, and how we treat others. When we follow Islamic law, we are guided to make good choices that please Allah.

Class activity:
Pupils will sort different actions into halal and haram categories and explain their choices.

Evaluation questions:
1. What does halal mean?
2. What does haram mean?
3. Give an example of something halal and something haram.
4. Where does Islamic law come from?

Summary:
Understanding halal and haram helps us make good choices in our daily lives according to Islamic teachings.

topics.title: Islamic civilisation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name important inventions by Muslim scholars.
The pupils should be able to explain the importance of knowledge in Islam.
The pupils should be able to identify contributions of Muslim scholars to world civilization.

Introduction:
Today we will learn about Islamic civilization and the great contributions of Muslim scholars to knowledge and invention. Islam encourages seeking knowledge and learning from the world around us.

Content:
Muslim scholars made many important contributions to civilization. They developed algebra, the number system we use today, and advanced medical knowledge. Muslim astronomers made detailed maps of the stars and invented instruments to study the sky. Muslim doctors wrote medical books that were used in Europe for hundreds of years. Libraries in cities like Baghdad, Cairo, and Cordoba were centers of learning where people from different religions studied together. The Prophet said: 'Seeking knowledge is an obligation on every Muslim.' These scholars showed us how Islam encourages learning and discovery.

Class activity:
Pupils will research and present on one Muslim scholar and their contribution to knowledge.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name one contribution of Muslim scholars to mathematics.
2. What did Muslim astronomers study?
3. What did the Prophet say about seeking knowledge?
4. Why were Islamic libraries important?

Summary:
Muslim scholars made many important contributions to world civilization, showing how Islam values knowledge and learning.

topics.title: Revision and recitation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite verses from Surah An - Naba.
The pupils should be able to explain the main points learned about hadith, fiqh, seerah, and Islamic law.
The pupils should be able to participate in a Quran recitation competition.

Introduction:
This week we will revise what we learned this term and practice our Quran recitation. Revision helps us remember important teachings and recitation brings us closer to Allah.

Content:
We will review Surah An - Naba, hadith on good character, rules of fasting and zakat, the Madinah community, peace treaties, halal and haram, and Islamic civilization. We will practice reciting Surah An - Naba with proper pronunciation and tajweed. We will also discuss how to apply these teachings in our daily lives. For example, how to have good character, how to fast properly, and how to make peace with others. This revision will help us remember and apply what we learned throughout the term.

Class activity:
Pupils will participate in a Quran recitation competition where they recite Surah An - Naba and are judged on pronunciation and memorization.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is the main theme of Surah An - Naba?
2. Why is good character important in Islam?
3. What are the rules of fasting in Ramadan?
4. How did the Prophet build peace in Madinah?
5. What does halal mean?

Summary:
Revision helps us remember and apply the Islamic teachings we learned this term, and recitation of the Quran brings us closer to Allah.
